previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of systolic and diastolic heart failure, atrial flutter s/p ablation, diabetes, and obesity was admitted for worsening dyspnea and lethargy after stopping his medications for four days due to financial constraints. He had recently been switched from metoprolol to atenolol, which likely contributed to asymptomatic hypotension in the ED. He was restarted on metoprolol 12.5 mg twice daily and furosemide 40 mg twice daily, with resolution of symptoms and stabilization of vital signs. His warfarin was resumed after a subtherapeutic INR, and diabetes management continued with insulin glargine and lispro. He remained in normal sinus rhythm throughout admission. Discharge was planned after two days with instructions to monitor weight, adhere to a low-salt diet, and follow up with primary care and specialty clinics.

#Acute Heart Failure: Patient presented with significant dyspnea

diuresed nearly 15 liters on the morning of ___. Pt left the 
hospital in mid ___. Did not wait to sign AMA form. Said he 
had ""business to attend to."" Would not wait for the attending.

  Since the patient began to have an increase in creatinine 
secondary to his diuresis, he was not started on an ace 
inhibitor in the inpatient. He is to follow up in the outpatient 
for further management.

# Atrial Fibrillation: Patient was in atrial fibrillation upon 
admission with rates in the low 100's. Metoprolol was uptitrated

this medication, and felt quite lightheaded. Unfortunately, he

he was ultimately TEE-DC cardioverted. A TEE was performed 
because the patient's INR was subtherapeutic upon admission. No 
clot was found. After his cardioversion, the patient remained 
mostly in sinus rhythm with brief episodes of atrial 
fibrillation the night of ___. 

 Since the patient left AMA, it is unclear what dosage of

advised to follow up with a cardio-net monitor to assess whether 
the patient's rhythm and to follow up with cardiology.

had no chest pain. Repeat cardiac troponin was unchanged at

from significant longstanding atrial fibrillation and volume 
overload. Patient's cardiac cath ___ showed clean coronaries.
